Measuring voice recordings with voice_acoustics.praat

A step-by-step tutorial

November 2026

This tutorial walks through Clinical Voice Snapshot (the script file voice_acoustics.praat), a Praat script that measures a sustained vowel /a/, six sentences and a conversational speech sample. It saves a results.json file for the rating web page, and optionally a spreadsheet for research and a plain-text summary for reports.

About the screenshots. They were taken in Praat 7.0.02 on Windows, with a short demo recording that contains one sustained /a/ and one sentence. Folder paths and the folder lists in the Windows file browsers are shortened or blurred. On a Mac the file browsers look different, but the Praat dialogs are the same.

1 Before you start

  • Praat. The script was developed for Praat 7.0.02. It also runs in older versions, but then it adds a warning to the results that the numbers may differ and that some measures may fail. Praat can be downloaded from praat.org.
  • The script file. Save voice_acoustics.praat anywhere, for example in your Downloads folder.
  • The recordings. The script reads .wav, .flac, .mp3, .aif, .aiff and .aifc files. You do not need to rename or move them.

The script works with recordings made in either of two ways:

Recorded as What that means Go to
Separate files One sound file per task: the vowel in one file, each sentence in its own file, the conversation in another. Path A
One recording All the tasks in one long sound file. The script guesses where the vowel and the sentences are, and you check its guesses. Path B

The tasks the script knows about:

Task How many Notes
Sustained vowel /a/ 1, plus up to 2 extra takes Ideally 3 to 5 seconds of steady voicing.
Sentences 1 to 6 6 Only the sentence numbers are shown, not their text.
Conversational speech 1, plus an optional second sample Not guessed automatically in Path B; you mark it yourself.

Recording quality matters. CPPS needs a sampling rate of at least 10,000 Hz. Formants need at least twice the formant ceiling of the speaker profile (for example 11,000 Hz for a 5,500 Hz ceiling). Ordinary recordings at 44,100 or 48,000 Hz are fine for every profile.

2 Open and run the script

  1. Start Praat. Two windows open, Praat Objects and Praat Picture. You can ignore or close the Picture window.
  2. In the Praat Objects window, open the Praat menu and choose Open Praat script…. Choose voice_acoustics.praat.
The Praat Objects window. Open Praat script… is in the Praat menu at the top left.
  1. The script opens in a script window. Don’t change anything in it.
  2. In the script window, choose Run > Run (or press Ctrl+R, or Cmd+R on a Mac).
The script window. The comments at the top repeat these instructions; use Run > Run in the menu bar.

3 The first dialog

The first dialog. Type a patient ID (optional), then click one of the two buttons.
  1. Patient ID (optional). It is written into the results. With separate files it is also used in the names of the results files, for example P001_results.json. Only letters, digits, - and _ are kept in file names.
  2. Click Separate files or One recording. Cancel stops the script.

4 Path A: separate files

4.1 Choose the folder

A folder browser opens. Choose the folder that contains the recordings and click OK. The results will be saved in this folder.

The folder browser on Windows (the folder list is blurred here).

If you close the browser without choosing a folder, or the folder has no sound files, the script asks whether to try another folder or to choose the files one by one.

4.2 Tell the script which file is which task

One dialog lists every task, each with a drop-down list of the sound files in the folder. If a file’s name looks like a task, the script fills it in for you (see file names it recognizes). Here it recognized P001_ah.wav as the vowel and P001_sentence1.wav as Sentence 1.

Check every filled-in file. Set any task that wasn’t recorded to (none).
  • Click a task’s box to choose its file from the list, or (none) if it wasn’t recorded.
  • Vowel 2, Vowel 3 and Conversation 2 are optional extra takes.
  • Other folder… lets you choose a different folder. One by one… switches to choosing each file separately.
  • Click OK when every task is right.

4.3 Alternative: choose the files one by one

If the recordings are in different folders, click One by one…. The script then asks for each task in turn (Task 1 of 8, Task 2 of 8, and so on).

One task at a time. If a file was already found, keep it with Use this.
  • Use this keeps the file shown, Other file… opens a file browser, and Remove clears the task.
  • When nothing is chosen yet, the buttons are Skip and Choose file….
  • Extra takes (vowel takes 2 and 3, conversation 2) are only asked for after the take before them was chosen. Click Skip if there isn’t one.

Now continue with Check the settings and run the analysis.

5 Path B: one recording with all the tasks

5.1 Choose the recording

A file browser opens. Choose the sound file that contains all the tasks and click Open.

Choosing the long recording (the folder list on the left is blurred here).

On Windows, Praat may now say “The phonetic font is not available”. Click OK. This only affects how phonetic symbols are drawn, not the analysis.

A harmless warning. Click OK.

5.2 Look at the script’s guesses

Two windows open: a sound window showing the recording, and the Mark the tasks dialog. The script has already looked for the sustained vowel and the sentences, and labelled what it found in the tasks row at the bottom of the sound window. It never guesses the conversation.

The sound window with the script’s guesses: the waveform at the top, the labelled marks in the yellow tasks row at the bottom. Zoom with the all / in / out / sel buttons at the bottom left. On Windows, the panel of phonetic symbols on the right can be closed with the small pink ✕ at its top right, or ignored.
The Mark the tasks dialog. The top line says what happened last; the Marked: line counts the marks for each kind of task.

Keep the sound window open until you click Done. The dialog works through the sound window, so if you close it, the script stops with an error and you have to start again.

How the guesses are made, and how to get better guesses

The script looks for stretches of sound with silence between them. A stretch counts as silence when it is at least 0.3 seconds long and more than 25 dB quieter than the loudest part of the recording. Each stretch of sound between silences is then sorted:

  • vowel /a/: at least 0.8 s long, mostly voiced (at least 60%), and with a steady pitch (a standard deviation of at most 1.5 semitones). If no stretch is that steady, for example with a very rough voice, the most voiced stretch that is at least 1.5 s long and at least 60% voiced is taken instead;
  • sentence: between 0.4 and 6 s long and at least 20% voiced;
  • anything else is left unmarked.

Up to 3 vowels and 6 sentences are marked, in recording order. Each mark is widened by 0.05 s on both sides.

Tip: leave clear pauses between the tasks. The guesses depend on finding silence between tasks, so the more silent padding there is between them, the better the guesses will be. Leave at least half a second, and ideally a second or more, of silence before and after each task, and keep background noise low. Tasks that run into each other with no pause become one long stretch, which is then too long or too uneven to be recognized as a vowel or a sentence.

Two things padding can’t fix. First, silence is judged relative to the loudest part of the recording, so steady background noise (a fan, a hum, a noisy room) within about 25 dB of the voice is not heard as silence, however long the pause. Second, a pause of 0.3 s or more inside a sentence splits it into two pieces, which may then be marked as two sentences. The guesses are only a starting point, so always check them.

5.3 Check each mark

  1. In the sound window, click the label of a mark (for example Sentence 1). The mark is selected and highlighted in pink.
  2. In the dialog, click Listen to hear that part.
  3. If the mark is wrong, click Remove. To remove several marks at once, drag across all of them in the sound window first.
Clicking a label selects its mark. The selected stretch, here 7.08 to 8.22 s, is what Listen plays and what Remove removes.
After Remove, the top line confirms what was removed, and the count goes down.

If you click Listen or Remove without anything selected, the dialog comes back with a PLEASE FIX line that says what to do:

A PLEASE FIX message: click the label of a mark first.

5.4 Add a mark

  1. In the sound window, drag the mouse across the task in the waveform, from just before it starts to just after it ends. Zoom in first (in, or sel to zoom to a selection) if you need more detail.
  2. In the dialog, under This part is, choose Vowel /a/, Sentence or Conversation.
  3. Click Mark.
A selection dragged across the sentence, from 7.06 to 8.33 s. A selection must be at least 0.25 s long, so a plain click is never taken as a mark.
The dialog confirms the new mark and its times. If it’s wrong, click Remove straight away.
The new mark in the tasks row.

Sentences are numbered in recording order. The first sentence mark in the recording becomes Sentence 1, the next Sentence 2, and so on. If a sentence wasn’t recorded, the sentences after it get lower numbers, so check the numbering in the summary (next step).

You can mark up to 3 vowels, 6 sentences and 2 conversation samples. Marks may overlap (for example, a sentence inside the conversation); the summary points this out.

5.5 Finish marking

When every mark is right, click Done.

6 Check the settings and run the analysis

The Check before the analysis dialog lists what will be analyzed: each file (separate files), or the times of each marked part (one recording).

Separate files: each task with its file, or (skipped).
One recording: each marked part with its times, plus a note when fewer than 6 sentences are marked.
  1. Speaker profile. The profile sets the pitch range and the formant ceiling used in the analysis. It starts at adult_female; choose the one that fits the speaker (see the profile table).
  2. Also save. Tick or untick the extra files: the spreadsheet for research (CSV) and the text summary. The results.json file is always saved; the rating web page only reads that one.
  3. Change files (separate files) or Edit marks (one recording) goes back to the previous step.
  4. Advanced… lets you change the analysis settings. Most people don’t need this. When something was changed, the dialog lists the changes.
  5. Click Run analysis.

If something is wrong (no file chosen, nothing marked, or a pitch floor above the pitch ceiling), the dialog comes back with a PLEASE FIX line explaining what to change.

6.1 Advanced settings

The Advanced settings window has two pages, so that it fits on small screens.

Advanced settings, page 1: pitch, formants and the vowel window. Leave the Hz values at 0 to use the speaker profile’s values.
Advanced settings, page 2: CPPS, intensity, HNR, jitter, shimmer and stereo channels. Click a box to see its choices.

The labels in the window are kept short so that they fit. This table explains each setting in full:

Page Setting Default Other choices
1 Pitch floor, pitch ceiling, formant ceiling (Hz) 0 = the speaker profile’s values any value
1 Number of formants 5 at least 3
1 Formant window whole_trimmed (mean, median and SD over the analyzed part) midpoint (one value at the middle)
1 Vowel window 3 s (the middle 3 s of the voiced vowel) any length above 0
1 Short vowel fraction 0.5 (the middle 50% of a vowel shorter than the window) above 0, at most 1
2 Preset for CPPS praat_default (the Get CPPS defaults of Praat 7.0.02) maryn_weenink_2015 (AVQI v02.02 settings)
2 Voiced parts only for speech CPPS / intensity on off (the whole recording)
2 Intensity averaging energy dB
2 Harmonicity method (HNR) cc (cross-correlation) ac (autocorrelation)
2 Period range (jitter, shimmer) derived (0.8 / pitch ceiling to 1.25 / pitch floor) fixed (0.1 to 20 ms, as in AVQI)
2 Jitter measures local local_absolute, rap, ppq5, ddp (comma-separated)
2 Shimmer measures local, local_db apq3, apq5, apq11, dda (comma-separated)
2 Stereo channels average left
  • Next > goes to page 2, and < Previous back to page 1. OK on page 2 keeps the changes.
  • Reset all shows the defaults again. Discard changes closes the window and keeps the values that were there when you opened it.
  • If a value isn’t allowed (for example fewer than 3 formants, or a jitter measure that doesn’t exist), the page comes back with a PLEASE FIX line.
  • Every value that was used is saved in the results, so a changed setting can always be seen afterwards.

7 Allow the script to save the results

When the analysis is done, Praat asks for permission before the script saves each file. Click the middle button, Yes, I allow this script to perform the action that it requests (and ask me again next time).

Praat’s safety check. The middle button allows only this save; CANCEL means the file is not saved.

Praat asks once for each file: up to four times per run (the results file, the two CSV files and the text summary), fewer if you unticked the extra files. There is no need to choose the third button.

8 Find the results and upload them

The Analysis finished dialog lists the files that were saved and the folder they are in. Click OK.

Separate files: the files are named after the patient ID.
One recording: the files are named after the recording, and your marks are saved next to them as a TextGrid.
File What it is Saved
<name>_results.json The results for the rating web page Always
<name>_results_long.csv One row per recording and measure, for R, Python, SPSS or Excel If ticked
<name>_parameters.csv The settings and analysis parameters used If ticked (with the CSV)
<name>_summary.txt The results as plain text, to read or paste into a report; also shown in the Praat Info window If ticked
<name>_marks.TextGrid Your marks, which you can open in Praat with the recording One recording only

<name> is the patient ID for separate files (voice without an ID), or the recording’s name for one recording. All the files are saved next to the recordings. An existing file is never replaced: if a name is already taken, _2, _3, and so on is added to all the files of that run.

Last step: on the rating web page, click Upload results.json and choose the _results.json file.

9 What is measured

Task Part analyzed Measures
Sustained /a/ The middle 3 s of the voiced part, so silence and noise before and after are ignored. If the voiced part is shorter than 3 s, the middle 50% of it, with a warning. F0 mean and SD; mean intensity; CPPS; HNR; jitter (local); shimmer (local, local dB); F1, F2, F3 mean, median and SD
Sentences, conversation The whole file or marked part. Intensity and CPPS use only the voiced stretches. F0 mean and SD; mean intensity; CPPS; voiced duration
  • Intensity is relative. It is uncalibrated dB, never dB SPL, so only compare it between recordings made with the same setup.
  • A measure that fails is never written as 0. It appears as null in the JSON file and NA in the CSV, with the reason.
  • Takes are not averaged. Each take is reported separately.
  • Warnings point out things worth checking: a vowel shorter than 3 s, or a pause of 0.1 s or more inside the vowel’s analysis window (a voice break, a cough, or noise detected as voicing).
  • CPPS is computed with Praat’s own Get CPPS defaults. The settings of the AVQI script (Maryn & Weenink, 2015) can be chosen instead under Advanced…. Jitter, shimmer and HNR follow the Praat manual. Other jitter and shimmer measures can also be added there.

9.1 Working with the results in R

The demo outputs are in the demo_output folder next to this tutorial. The spreadsheet is in “long” format: one row per recording and measure. Every row repeats the patient ID and the settings, so the files of several speakers can simply be stacked.

res <- read.csv(file.path(demo, "P001_all_tasks_results_long.csv"))
dim(res)
## [1] 21 22
names(res)
##  [1] "speakerID"         "speakerProfile"    "pitchFloorHz"     
##  [4] "pitchCeilingHz"    "formantCeilingHz"  "cppsMethod"       
##  [7] "runDate"           "scriptVersion"     "praatVersion"     
## [10] "fileName"          "task"              "take"             
## [13] "status"            "durationSec"       "sampleRateHz"     
## [16] "analysisStartSec"  "analysisEndSec"    "voicedDurationSec"
## [19] "measure"           "value"             "unit"             
## [22] "missingReason"

The measures of the demo recording:

A measure that could not be computed is NA, and the missingReason column says why. In the demo, every measure worked:

sum(is.na(res$value))
## [1] 0

With your own recordings, list the missing measures and their reasons like this:

subset(res, is.na(value), select = c(fileName, task, measure, missingReason))

To get one row per recording and one column per measure (a “wide” table):

wide <- reshape(res[, c("speakerID", "task", "take", "measure", "value")],
                idvar = c("speakerID", "task", "take"),
                timevar = "measure", direction = "wide")
names(wide) <- sub("^value\\.", "", names(wide))
wide[, c("speakerID", "task", "take", "f0Mean", "f0SD", "cpps")]
speakerID task take f0Mean f0SD cpps
1 P001 vowel_a 1 223.45 1.99 16.61
18 P001 sentence_1 1 202.51 74.98 9.82

To combine several speakers, read every _results_long.csv file in a folder and stack them:

files <- list.files("my_results_folder", pattern = "_results_long\\.csv$",
                    full.names = TRUE)
all_results <- do.call(rbind, lapply(files, read.csv))

The text summary lists the same values in a readable form. Here is its part for the sustained vowel:

summary_lines <- readLines(file.path(demo, "P001_all_tasks_summary.txt"))
start <- which(summary_lines == "Sustained /a/")
cat(summary_lines[start:(start + 19)], sep = "\n")
## Sustained /a/

10 Troubleshooting

What you see What to do
“The phonetic font is not available” Click OK. It doesn’t affect the analysis.
“Cancelled. Nothing was analyzed. Script exited.” You clicked Cancel or closed a dialog. Run the script again with Run > Run.
A PLEASE FIX line at the top of a dialog Do what it says, then click the button again.
“No recordings found” after choosing a folder The folder has no sound files with a supported extension. Choose another folder, or click One by one….
A file wasn’t filled in automatically Its name doesn’t look like a task. Choose it from the list by hand.
“Praat could not open … as a sound” The file is damaged or isn’t really a sound file. Choose another file. With separate files, the results list it with status error.
The script found few or no tasks in one recording There are probably no clear pauses between the tasks, or the background is noisy. Mark the tasks by hand (see how the guesses are made).
A sentence was split into two marks It contains a pause of 0.3 s or more. Remove both marks, drag across the whole sentence, and click Mark.
“nothing is selected” after Listen or Mark Click a label, or drag across a part, in the sound window first.
“the sentence marks are all used (6)” Remove one first, then add the new one.
Warning: the voiced part of the vowel is shorter than 3 s Only the middle 50% was analyzed. If possible, use a longer /a/ take.
A measure is null / NA because the sample rate is too low Re-record or export at 44,100 or 48,000 Hz.
Praat says its version is older than the tested version The results may differ from Praat 7.0.02. Update Praat if you can.

11 Reference

11.1 Speaker profiles

Profile Pitch floor Pitch ceiling Formant ceiling
adult_female (default) 100 Hz 500 Hz 5,500 Hz
child 100 Hz 600 Hz 8,000 Hz
adult_male 75 Hz 300 Hz 5,000 Hz
trans_woman 75 Hz 500 Hz 5,250 Hz
trans_man 75 Hz 500 Hz 5,250 Hz
other_unspecified 75 Hz 600 Hz 5,250 Hz

Values set under Advanced… replace the profile’s values, and the results record that they were changed.

11.2 File names the script recognizes (separate files)

Upper or lower case doesn’t matter, and anything else in the name (such as a patient ID) is ignored. These are only first guesses, and you can always change them in the list.

Task Names that are recognized
Sustained /a/ contains vowel or sustain, or a separate word a, ah or aah (e.g. P001_ah.wav, vowel_a.wav)
Sentence 1 to 6 sentence or sent followed by the number (e.g. sentence3.wav, P001_sent_3.wav)
Conversation contains conv, extemp, spont, monolog, narrat, sandwich, pbj or family
Extra takes the name ends in _t2, _take2 or _take_2 (e.g. ah_t2.wav)
Not filled in /i/ vowels (vowel_i, ee, i), which are not part of these tasks

Written for Clinical Voice Snapshot (voice_acoustics.praat) version 0.1.0 (results format 0.2.0), tested in Praat 7.0.02.
